output.title: Spot trial expiry before it becomes a surprise
output.body:
If you run a small business, trial expiry is a workflow decision, not a grand AI project: when should a reminder fire, and who should see it first? The useful question is simple. Are your trial dates already in one digital place—calendar, email, spreadsheet, or CRM—or are they scattered across vendor accounts? If they are central, a light monitoring rule may be enough. If they are scattered, you are probably looking at a small integration job, not a full overhaul.

The control stays human. Automation should surface the date; the owner still decides whether to renew, downgrade, or cancel. That matters because money movement and other high-risk decisions should stay with a person. AI can help you notice the deadline, but it should not quietly choose the plan. That is a tidy way to buy the wrong thing.

A practical next step is to list every SaaS trial you are using and mark which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. Then note whether the reminder needs to arrive 30 days out, 7 days out, or at some other threshold you choose. That inventory tells you whether the work is simple monitoring or a small workflow change in your own environment. Bareni starts with that one recurring workflow and keeps the scope bounded.
